evals.expected_output: Lists the seven log groups with STANDARD class; /aws/vpc/flowlogs-prod and /app/tiny-tool show Never expire; the others show their retentionInDays.

evals.prompt: Read cloudwatch-context.json. Using the CloudWatch cost optimization skill, what effective rate per GB should be used to size Standard log ingestion savings for October 2026, and which Cost Explorer rows feed it? Show the arithmetic.
evals.expected_output: $0.50 per GB: $3,000 ÷ 6,000 GB from USE1-DataProcessing-Bytes only. The Global-DataProcessing-Bytes row (5 GB at $0) is free-tier usage and is excluded from the rate.

assertions.text: gives a rate of 0.50 per GB

evals.prompt: Read cloudwatch-context.json. Following the CloudWatch cost optimization skill, estimate how many GB of stored data a 90-day retention policy would remove from /aws/vpc/flowlogs-prod, and say how confident the estimate is. Show the method.
evals.expected_output: old_share = 48,000 ÷ 60,000 = 0.8 of the ingestion history is older than 90 days; GB removed ≈ 2,000 × 0.8 ≈ 1,600 GB. The group was created in 2023, before the 15-month history, so this is a lower bound.
assertions: The response derives the share older than 90 days from the ingestion history (48,000 of 60,000, or 80%)
The response says the estimate is a lower bound because the log group is older than the available metric history
The response does not assume that all 2,000 GB of storedBytes would be removed

evals.prompt: Read cloudwatch-context.json. Using the CloudWatch cost optimization skill's eligibility rules, which log groups are candidates for the Essentials (formerly Infrequent Access) log class, and why is each of the others excluded?
evals.expected_output: Candidates: /app/batch-archive and /aws/vpc/flowlogs-prod (vended-log destinations qualify). Excluded: /aws/lambda/orders-api (metric filters), /ecs/payments (EMF metrics), /aws/containerinsights/prod-eks/performance (Container Insights performance logs), /app/search-api (field index). /app/tiny-tool is too small to matter. The class can't be changed, so each move needs a new log group.
assertions: The response identifies /app/batch-archive as a candidate
The response identifies /aws/vpc/flowlogs-prod as a candidate or explicitly allows vended-log destinations
The response excludes /aws/lambda/orders-api because it has metric filters
The response excludes /ecs/payments because it carries embedded metric format (EMF) metrics
The response excludes /app/search-api because it has a field index, which Essentials does not support
The response states that the log class cannot be changed after creation, so a new log group is needed

evals.prompt: Read cloudwatch-context.json. Total CloudWatch spend for October 2026 is about $9,300. Using the CloudWatch cost optimization skill's severity rules, what severity does (a) dropping the PodName dimension from Checkout/Latency get if it saves $1,500 a month, and (b) setting retention on /app/tiny-tool get? Explain using the thresholds.
evals.expected_output: (a) CRITICAL: $1,500 is about 16% of CloudWatch spend (≥10%) and MetricMonitorUsage grew in each of the last two complete months (2,700 → 4,000 → 6,000). (b) INFO: the group holds about 3 MB, so the saving is effectively zero after the free tier.
assertions: The response rates the PodName dimension finding CRITICAL
The response justifies CRITICAL with the saving being at least 10% of CloudWatch spend and MetricMonitorUsage growing in each of the last two months
The response rates the /app/tiny-tool retention finding INFO, not HIGH or MEDIUM

evals.prompt: Read cloudwatch-context.json. GetMetricData (GMD-Metrics) cost $1,500 in October. Following the CloudWatch cost optimization skill, who is calling GetMetricData, and how do you know?
evals.expected_output: It can't be confirmed: GetMetricData is a CloudTrail data event, and the only trail logs S3 data events, so no record of callers exists and LookupEvents (Event history) can't show it. monitoring-integration-role trusts an external account and is a likely candidate; ask the user which monitoring tools poll CloudWatch, and recommend a longer polling interval or a metric stream.
assertions: The response says the caller cannot be confirmed from CloudTrail because GetMetricData is a data event that is not being recorded
The response does not claim to have found the caller through LookupEvents or CloudTrail Event history
The response names monitoring-integration-role as a possible caller rather than a confirmed one
The response asks the user which tools poll CloudWatch or recommends confirming before acting

evals.prompt: Read cloudwatch-context.json. Write only the Executive Summary section of the CloudWatch cost optimization report for a head of platform engineering, following the skill's report template. Use the data in the file; where a saving needs a decision you can't make, say so.
evals.expected_output: A short, plain-language summary: monthly and annualized CloudWatch spend, its share of total AWS spend (about 9%), savings split into no-visibility-impact and needs-a-decision, a Decisions needed list (for example retention requirement for flow logs, the on-call paging alarm), and at most 5 top actions with owner and S/M/L effort.
assertions: The response gives both monthly and annualized figures
The response states CloudWatch's share of total AWS spend
The response includes a Decisions needed list
The response lists top actions with an owner (or 'unassigned') and an effort size
The response does not quote a CloudWatch list price that isn't derived from the file
